title: Recover Binary Search Tree
description:
You are given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST) where the values of **exactly two** nodes of the tree were swapped by mistake. Recover the tree **in-place** without changing its structure (only swap the values of the two misplaced nodes).

Your method should not return anything; modify the tree rooted at `root` directly. Can you solve it in `O(1)` auxiliary space?
constraints: 2 <= number of nodes in the tree <= 1000
All values in the tree are unique.
Exactly two nodes in the BST have had their values swapped.
hints: The inorder traversal of a valid BST produces values in strictly ascending order. Swapping two nodes introduces either one inversion (if they are adjacent in inorder) or two inversions (if they are non-adjacent).
Track the previously visited node prev during inorder traversal. Whenever prev.val > curr.val, set first = prev (only on the first inversion) and always update second = curr.

To achieve O(1) extra space instead of O(h) recursion/stack space, perform Morris Inorder Traversal and make sure to finish restoring all temporary right-pointer threads before swapping first.val and second.val.

examples.explanation: Inorder traversal is [3, 2, 1], showing inversions at (3, 2) and (2, 1). Swapping 3 and 1 restores the valid BST [3, 1, null, null, 2].
Inorder traversal is [1, 3, 2, 4], showing a single adjacent inversion (3, 2). Swapping 3 and 2 restores [2, 1, 4, null, null, 3].
Nodes 3 and 1 are swapped; swapping their values back restores [2, 1, 3].
